behavior.primary: Strict correct-versus-finished-wrong-object disagreement counts, pair rates and affected-world prevalence, separately for both models.
behavior.reporting: Keep the complete fixed grid, all errors, all worlds and both models; no favorable subgroup replaces the primary result.

case_selection.eligibility: Donor strictly correct on all three facts and its identity; recipient has at least one finished wrong-object fact. All initially wrong recipient facts count, not only the screening fact.
case_selection.scope: Conditional on eligible correct-source/wrong-recipient contexts in the same 64 worlds used for behavior; not a second independent dataset.
case_selection.selection: Old SHA256 world/context/screen-field ordering, applied to every eligible confirmation world using only unchanged answers.

completion: Report completed, failed and incomplete stages regardless of outcome. A compute deadline or insufficient sample is not evidence that the repair never works; no further search is automatically authorized.
execution: Publish and freeze this protocol, complete source closure, input digests and model pins before the first pretrained confirmation forward. Require separate bounded spending approval, a recorded deadline and sufficient persistent storage. Do not alter archived runners or their development-only guards.

generation.answer_rule: Complete decoded response with case/whitespace/final punctuation normalization; unfinished responses and explanations remain errors.

numeric.unsupported_or_failed_oracle: Stop the registered repair stage and retain the failure; no smoothing, case replacement, head search or relaxed tolerance.

old_results_preserved: The 1/8 development repair and failed follow-up remain failed; this new plan does not promote either to success.
overall_utility: Report point-estimate practical requirements separately: world-balanced repair at least 0.50, advantage over frozen mean at least 0.25, and protected-world damage at most 0.10. The 0.25 advantage is a newly specified world-balanced comparison, not a redefinition of the earlier pooled 2/8 gate. Separate individual 95% intervals do not establish a simultaneous 95% overall-utility claim; no positive overall claim is automatically authorized.
preservation: Report damaged protected facts and worlds separately. Compute an exact one-sided 95% binomial-reference upper bound on affected-world risk. A 10% risk threshold is reported, never assumed from zero observed damage.
purpose: Independent behavioral repetition and estimation of one unchanged failed repair candidate.

repair.baseline: Saved complete unmodified behavior, not an extra condition chosen after intervention outcomes.
repair.generation: One first-step delta per destination question, reused at its original query position for all recomputed greedy steps; no cache or teacher forcing.
repair.preserved: Recipient total record attention, within-record relative token weights, nonrecord attention and recipient value vectors.
repair.primary: Copy the correct donor's color-question record shares unchanged across the three recipient property questions.

statistics.family_scope: Each interval is individual, not simultaneous across models, endpoints or controls. No family-wide confidence or significance claim.
statistics.repair_bounds: Hoeffding bounded-world mean intervals on [0,1]; paired primary-minus-frozen-mean intervals on [-1,1], under the stated sampling approximation.
statistics.sampling_assumption: Intervals use an independent-world sampling approximation for this artificial task generator. Balanced margins and unique field assignments couple the generated worlds, so these are model-based reference intervals, not unconditional guarantees. Fixed-sample counts are exact descriptive results. Neither repeated questions nor the two models create additional independent worlds.
statistics.world_prevalence: Two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson binomial reference bounds, including nonzero bounds after zero observed events.

usefulness_decision: With at least 20 eligible worlds: the targeted repair fraction is excluded only if the conservative 95% bounded-world upper interval is below 0.50; above-threshold repair benefit alone is supported only if its lower interval is at least 0.50; otherwise uncertain. Benefit alone is not a useful overall fix if it damages correct answers or lacks an advantage over the frozen-mean control. With fewer than 20 worlds report imprecision, not a qualified candidate.
usefulness_estimand: Mean across eligible worlds of the fraction of that world's initially wrong recipient facts repaired. This world-balanced estimand differs from the earlier pooled 4/8 engineering target; both are reported, but the old gate is not redefined.
